semantically_equivalent_domains.justification: Clinical neurophysiology is a specific application of neurophysiology in a clinical setting, and neurophysiology is part of the larger scientific study of the nervous system, in paraticular this domain seems closely related.

parent_domains.justification: Clinical Neurophysiology is a branch of neuroscience that deals particularly with the study and understanding of the structure and function of the nervous system.
Clinical Neurophysiology is closely related to neurology, as it involves studying and diagnosing neurological disorders through electrophysiological techniques.
Electrophysiology is a core method applied within clinical neurophysiology for the study of electrical properties of biological cells and tissues.

closest_parent_domain.justification: Electrophysiology is most directly connected to clinical neurophysiology as the clinical discipline often involves the measurement and interpretation of electrical activity in the nervous system.

child_domains.justification: Electroencephalography is a sub-discipline under clinical neurophysiology that specifically involves recording electrical activity along the scalp produced by the firing of neurons.

closest_child_domain.justification: Electroencephalography most directly relates to clinical neurophysiology as it is a common technique used within this field to measure brain wave patterns.

sibling_domains.justification: Clinical Neurophysiology and neuroimaging are closely related, both involve diagnostic processes concerning the brain's function.
Functional neuroimaging is related to clinical neurophysiology as it provides visualization of brain activity, which complements the electrical data obtained through clinical neurophysiology.

closest_sibling_domain.justification: Functional neuroimaging is closely related as it provides a complementary perspective to the electrical recordings in clinical neurophysiology by adding visual data regarding brain activity.

unrelated_domains.justification: Neuroanatomy focuses more on the structure of the nervous system rather than its electrical activity and function, which is the focus of clinical neurophysiology.

Cognitive neuroscience focuses on the neural connections in the brain that are involved in mental processes, whereas clinical neurophysiology is more focused on measuring brain responses and diagnosing neurological disorders.
Visual neuroscience focuses specifically on the visual processing in the nervous system and is less connected to the broader diagnostic techniques in clinical neurophysiology.
Neuroergonomics focuses on the application of neuroscience to the design of technologies and tasks, which is different from the diagnostic focus of clinical neurophysiology.
Physiological psychology focuses on the physiological processes underlying behavior, which is distinct from the clinical diagnostic focus of neurophysiology.
Neuropsychology deals with how brain function affects behavior and cognition, which is distinct from the techniques used in clinical neurophysiology.
Neuropsychiatry deals with mental disorders attributable to diseases of the nervous system, which involves a broader range of techniques and focus than clinical neurophysiology.

Computational neuroscience focuses on both the theoretical and computational understanding of nervous system function, which is distinct from the more observational and diagnostic nature of clinical neurophysiology.
Theoretical neuroscience is focused on developing theoretical methods to understand neural systems, which differs from the clinical observational focus of clinical neurophysiology.
Neurotopology primarily involves the mapping of neural structures or activities and does not directly relate to the clinical or diagnostic focus of neurophysiology.
